title: Warehouse Ledger: Bulk Adjustments
description:
A warehouse keeps N shelves in a row; shelf i holds ai items (a negative number means items are owed). The manager issues Q commands: either add v items to every shelf from l to r, or report the total number of items on shelves l to r. Both kinds of command must be fast: a loop over the range is too slow.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N, Q ≤ 25000
  • |ai|, |v| ≤ 109
  • 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ N

Input

The first line contains N Q. The second line contains a1 … aN. Each of the next Q lines is either 1 l r v (add v to shelves l..r) or 2 l r (query the sum of shelves l..r).

Output

Let ans1, ans2, …, anst be the answers to the type-2 queries, in order. To keep the output small, print a single integer: the checksum (1·ans1 + 2·ans2 + … + t·anst) mod 1000000007, taken as a non-negative remainder (exactly what Python's % gives). If t = 0, print 0.

Example

Input:
5 5
1 2 3 4 5
2 1 5
1 2 4 10
2 1 3
1 1 5 -3
2 4 5

Output:
106

In this example the individual answers are 15, 26, 13, so the checksum is 1·15 + 2·26 + 3·13 mod 1000000007 = 106.
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, q = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    pre = [0] * (n + 1)
    s = 0
    for i in range(n):
        s += int(d[2 + i]); pre[i + 1] = s
    B1 = [0] * (n + 2); B2 = [0] * (n + 2)
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    p = 2 + n
    t = 0; res = 0
    for _ in range(q):
        if d[p] == b'1':
            l = int(d[p + 1]); r = int(d[p + 2]); v = int(d[p + 3]); p += 4
            i = l; w = v * (l - 1)
            while i <= n:
                B1[i] += v; B2[i] += w; i += i & -i
            i = r + 1; w = v * r
            while i <= n:
                B1[i] -= v; B2[i] -= w; i += i & -i
        else:
            l = int(d[p + 1]); r = int(d[p + 2]); p += 3
            def pref(x):
                a = b = 0; i = x
                while i > 0:
                    a += B1[i]; b += B2[i]; i -= i & -i
                return pre[x] + a * x - b
            ans = pref(r) - pref(l - 1)
            t += 1
            res = (res + t * ans) % MOD
    print(res)
main()

title: Temperature Spread Queries
description:
A weather station recorded N temperature readings. Scientists ask Q questions of the form “what is the spread (maximum minus minimum) of the readings from day l to day r?”. The data never changes, so preprocess it so each question is answered in O(1).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N, Q ≤ 70000
  • |ai| ≤ 109
  • 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ N

Input

The first line contains N Q, the second line the N readings, and each of the next Q lines a query l r.

Output

Let ans1, ans2, …, anst be the answers to the queries, in order. To keep the output small, print a single integer: the checksum (1·ans1 + 2·ans2 + … + t·anst) mod 1000000007, taken as a non-negative remainder (exactly what Python's % gives). If t = 0, print 0.

Example

Input:
6 4
3 -1 4 1 -5 9
1 3
2 5
4 4
1 6

Output:
79

In this example the individual answers are 5, 9, 0, 14, so the checksum is 1·5 + 2·9 + 3·0 + 4·14 mod 1000000007 = 79.
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, q = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    a = list(map(int, d[2:2 + n]))
    mn = [a]; mx = [a]; j = 1
    while 2 * j <= n:
        pm = mn[-1]; px = mx[-1]
        mn.append(list(map(min, pm, pm[j:])))
        mx.append(list(map(max, px, px[j:])))
        j *= 2
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    res = 0
    Qs = list(map(int, d[2 + n:2 + n + 2 * q]))
    t = 0
    for l, r in zip(Qs[0::2], Qs[1::2]):
        l -= 1; t += 1
        k = (r - l).bit_length() - 1
        m1 = mn[k]; m2 = mx[k]; o = r - (1 << k)
        lo = m1[l] if m1[l] < m1[o] else m1[o]
        hi = m2[l] if m2[l] > m2[o] else m2[o]
        res = (res + t * (hi - lo)) % MOD
    print(res)
main()

title: Equal Watchtowers
description:
Along a border stand N watchtowers with heights h1 … hN. Two towers i < j can signal each other if they have the same height and no tower strictly between them is taller than they are. Count the pairs of towers that can signal each other.

An O(N2) scan is too slow; a monotonic stack with counts solves it in O(N).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 200000
  • 1 ≤ hi ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains N; the second line contains the N heights.

Output

Print the number of pairs (it may exceed 231).

Example

Input:
7
2 1 2 3 2 2 3

Output:
3

title: Collapsing Bridges
description:
An archipelago has N islands and M bridges (bridge i joins islands ui and vi; a bridge may join an island to itself and two bridges may join the same pair). A storm destroys Q distinct bridges one after another. After each destruction, how many connected groups of islands are there?

Hint: union-find cannot delete edges… but it can add them. Process the destruction list backwards.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N, M ≤ 60000
  • 0 ≤ Q ≤ M
  • Bridge indices in the destruction list are distinct.

Input

The first line contains N M. Each of the next M lines contains a bridge u v (bridges are numbered 1..M in input order). The next line contains Q, and the last line contains the Q bridge numbers in destruction order (the line is empty when Q = 0).

Output

Let ans1, ans2, …, anst be the answers to the destructions (ansi = number of connected groups right after the i-th destruction), in order. To keep the output small, print a single integer: the checksum (1·ans1 + 2·ans2 + … + t·anst) mod 1000000007, taken as a non-negative remainder (exactly what Python's % gives). If t = 0, print 0.

Example

Input:
5 5
1 2
2 3
3 1
4 5
2 4
3
5 1 2

Output:
15

In this example the individual answers are 2, 2, 3, so the checksum is 1·2 + 2·2 + 3·3 mod 1000000007 = 15.
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, m = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    U = d[2:2 + 2 * m:2]; V = d[3:3 + 2 * m:2]
    p = 2 + 2 * m
    q = int(d[p]); rem = [int(x) - 1 for x in d[p + 1:p + 1 + q]]
    gone = [False] * m
    for e in rem: gone[e] = True
    par = list(range(n + 1))
    def find(x):
        while par[x] != x:
            par[x] = par[par[x]]; x = par[x]
        return x
    comps = n
    for e in range(m):
        if not gone[e]:
            a = find(int(U[e])); b = find(int(V[e]))
            if a != b: par[a] = b; comps -= 1
    ans = [0] * q
    for i in range(q - 1, -1, -1):
        ans[i] = comps
        e = rem[i]
        a = find(int(U[e])); b = find(int(V[e]))
        if a != b: par[a] = b; comps -= 1
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    print(sum((i + 1) * x for i, x in enumerate(ans)) % MOD)
main()

title: Budget Shoppers
description:
A street has N shops in a row; shop i sells its only item for ai coins (prices may be negative: the shop pays you). Each of Q shoppers walks from shop l to shop r with a budget of x coins and wants to know how many of those shops have a price at most x.

Hint: answer the queries offline in increasing order of x.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N, Q ≤ 30000
  • |ai|, |x| ≤ 109
  • 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ N

Input

The first line contains N, the second the N prices, the third Q; each of the next Q lines contains l r x.

Output

Let ans1, ans2, …, anst be the answers to the shoppers, in order. To keep the output small, print a single integer: the checksum (1·ans1 + 2·ans2 + … + t·anst) mod 1000000007, taken as a non-negative remainder (exactly what Python's % gives). If t = 0, print 0.

Example

Input:
5
4 1 3 5 2
3
1 5 3
2 4 2
3 3 2

Output:
5

In this example the individual answers are 3, 1, 0, so the checksum is 1·3 + 2·1 + 3·0 mod 1000000007 = 5.
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(d[0]); a = list(map(int, d[1:1 + n]))
    q = int(d[1 + n]); p = 2 + n
    L = [0] * q; Rr = [0] * q; X = [0] * q
    for i in range(q):
        L[i] = int(d[p]); Rr[i] = int(d[p + 1]); X[i] = int(d[p + 2]); p += 3
    order = sorted(range(n), key=a.__getitem__)
    qo = sorted(range(q), key=X.__getitem__)
    B = [0] * (n + 1)
    ans = [0] * q
    k = 0
    for qi in qo:
        x = X[qi]
        while k < n and a[order[k]] <= x:
            i = order[k] + 1
            while i <= n:
                B[i] += 1; i += i & -i
            k += 1
        s = 0; i = Rr[qi]
        while i > 0:
            s += B[i]; i -= i & -i
        i = L[qi] - 1
        while i > 0:
            s -= B[i]; i -= i & -i
        ans[qi] = s
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    print(sum((i + 1) * v for i, v in enumerate(ans)) % MOD)
main()

title: Bracket Repair Shop
description:
You are given a string of N brackets, each ( or ), and Q operations:

  • 1 i: flip the bracket at position i (( becomes ) and vice versa);
  • 2 l r: report the length of the longest regular bracket subsequence of the substring s[l..r] (a subsequence keeps the order of characters but may skip some; a regular sequence is a correctly matched one such as (()())).

A segment tree whose nodes store (matched length, unmatched (, unmatched )) answers each operation in O(log N). Careful: merging is not commutative.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N, Q ≤ 30000
  • 1 ≤ i ≤ N, 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ N

Input

The first line contains N Q, the second the bracket string, then Q lines with operations.

Output

Let ans1, ans2, …, anst be the answers to the type-2 operations, in order. To keep the output small, print a single integer: the checksum (1·ans1 + 2·ans2 + … + t·anst) mod 1000000007, taken as a non-negative remainder (exactly what Python's % gives). If t = 0, print 0.

Example

Input:
8 5
())(())(
2 1 8
2 2 3
1 3
2 1 8
2 1 4

Output:
32

In this example the individual answers are 6, 0, 6, 2, so the checksum is 1·6 + 2·0 + 3·6 + 4·2 mod 1000000007 = 32.
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, q = int(d[0]), int(d[1]); s = d[2]
    size = 1
    while size < n: size *= 2
    M = [0] * (2 * size); O = [0] * (2 * size); C = [0] * (2 * size)
    for i in range(n):
        if s[i] == 40: O[size + i] = 1
        else: C[size + i] = 1
    def pull(p):
        l = 2 * p; r = l + 1
        t = O[l] if O[l] < C[r] else C[r]
        M[p] = M[l] + M[r] + 2 * t; O[p] = O[l] + O[r] - t; C[p] = C[l] + C[r] - t
    for p in range(size - 1, 0, -1): pull(p)
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    res = 0; cnt = 0; k = 3
    for _ in range(q):
        if d[k] == b'1':
            i = int(d[k + 1]) - 1 + size; k += 2
            O[i], C[i] = C[i], O[i]
            i >>= 1
            while i:
                pull(i); i >>= 1
        else:
            l = int(d[k + 1]) - 1 + size; r = int(d[k + 2]) + size; k += 3
            am = ao = ac = 0
            rights = []
            while l < r:
                if l & 1:
                    t = ao if ao < C[l] else C[l]
                    am += M[l] + 2 * t; ao += O[l] - t; ac += C[l] - t
                    l += 1
                if r & 1:
                    r -= 1; rights.append(r)
                l >>= 1; r >>= 1
            for x in reversed(rights):
                t = ao if ao < C[x] else C[x]
                am += M[x] + 2 * t; ao += O[x] - t; ac += C[x] - t
            cnt += 1
            res = (res + cnt * am) % MOD
    print(res)
main()

title: Best Streak with Edits
description:
A trader's daily profits are a1 … aN (losses are negative). The records get corrected over time, and analysts keep asking for the best streak inside a period: the maximum sum of a non-empty contiguous block of days within [l, r].

  • 1 i v: set ai = v;
  • 2 l r: report the maximum non-empty subarray sum inside a[l..r].

Kadane's algorithm per query is O(N) — too slow. Store (total, best prefix, best suffix, best) in a segment tree.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N, Q ≤ 20000
  • |ai|, |v| ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains N Q, the second the N profits, then Q operation lines.

Output

Let ans1, ans2, …, anst be the answers to the type-2 operations (answers may be negative), in order. To keep the output small, print a single integer: the checksum (1·ans1 + 2·ans2 + … + t·anst) mod 1000000007, taken as a non-negative remainder (exactly what Python's % gives). If t = 0, print 0.

Example

Input:
6 5
2 -3 4 -1 2 -6
2 1 6
2 1 2
1 2 5
2 1 6
2 6 6

Output:
21

In this example the individual answers are 5, 2, 12, -6, so the checksum is 1·5 + 2·2 + 3·12 + 4·(-6) mod 1000000007 = 21.
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, q = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    size = 1
    while size < n: size *= 2
    NEG = -(10**18)
    S = [0] * (2 * size); P = [NEG] * (2 * size); Sf = [NEG] * (2 * size); B = [NEG] * (2 * size)
    for i in range(n):
        v = int(d[2 + i]); j = size + i
        S[j] = P[j] = Sf[j] = B[j] = v
    def pull(p):
        l = 2 * p; r = l + 1
        S[p] = S[l] + S[r]
        x = S[l] + P[r]; P[p] = P[l] if P[l] > x else x
        x = S[r] + Sf[l]; Sf[p] = Sf[r] if Sf[r] > x else x
        x = Sf[l] + P[r]
        b = B[l] if B[l] > B[r] else B[r]
        B[p] = b if b > x else x
    for p in range(size - 1, 0, -1): pull(p)
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    res = 0; cnt = 0; k = 2 + n
    for _ in range(q):
        if d[k] == b'1':
            j = int(d[k + 1]) - 1 + size; v = int(d[k + 2]); k += 3
            S[j] = P[j] = Sf[j] = B[j] = v
            j >>= 1
            while j:
                pull(j); j >>= 1
        else:
            l = int(d[k + 1]) - 1 + size; r = int(d[k + 2]) + size; k += 3
            left = []; rights = []
            while l < r:
                if l & 1: left.append(l); l += 1
                if r & 1: r -= 1; rights.append(r)
                l >>= 1; r >>= 1
            nodes = left + rights[::-1]
            x = nodes[0]
            s, pf, sf, b = S[x], P[x], Sf[x], B[x]
            for y in nodes[1:]:
                t = sf + P[y]
                if B[y] > b: b = B[y]
                if t > b: b = t
                t = s + P[y]
                if t > pf: pf = t
                t = S[y] + sf
                sf = Sf[y] if Sf[y] > t else t
                s += S[y]
            cnt += 1
            res = (res + cnt * b) % MOD
    print(res)
main()

title: Reservoir Levels
description:
A chain of N reservoirs has water levels a1 … aN (relative to sea level, so they may be negative). Rain and drought change the level of a whole block of consecutive reservoirs at once, and engineers need the lowest level within a block.

  • 1 l r v: add v to every level in [l, r];
  • 2 l r: report min(al, …, ar).

This needs a segment tree with lazy propagation (range add, range minimum).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N, Q ≤ 20000
  • |ai|, |v| ≤ 109
  • 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ N

Input

The first line contains N Q, the second the initial levels, then Q operation lines.

Output

Let ans1, ans2, …, anst be the answers to the type-2 operations (answers may be negative), in order. To keep the output small, print a single integer: the checksum (1·ans1 + 2·ans2 + … + t·anst) mod 1000000007, taken as a non-negative remainder (exactly what Python's % gives). If t = 0, print 0.

Example

Input:
5 5
3 1 4 1 5
2 1 5
1 2 4 3
2 1 5
2 2 4
2 5 5

Output:
39

In this example the individual answers are 1, 3, 4, 5, so the checksum is 1·1 + 2·3 + 3·4 + 4·5 mod 1000000007 = 39.
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, q = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    size = 1; h = 0
    while size < n: size *= 2; h += 1
    INF = 1 << 62
    t = [INF] * (2 * size); dd = [0] * size
    for i in range(n): t[size + i] = int(d[2 + i])
    for p in range(size - 1, 0, -1):
        t[p] = t[2 * p] if t[2 * p] < t[2 * p + 1] else t[2 * p + 1]
    def build(p):
        while p > 1:
            p >>= 1
            a = t[2 * p]; b = t[2 * p + 1]
            t[p] = (a if a < b else b) + dd[p]
    def push(p):
        for s in range(h, 0, -1):
            i = p >> s
            v = dd[i]
            if v:
                c = 2 * i
                t[c] += v; t[c + 1] += v
                if c < size: dd[c] += v; dd[c + 1] += v
                dd[i] = 0
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    res = 0; cnt = 0; k = 2 + n
    for _ in range(q):
        if d[k] == b'1':
            l = int(d[k + 1]) - 1 + size; r = int(d[k + 2]) + size; v = int(d[k + 3]); k += 4
            l0, r0 = l, r
            while l < r:
                if l & 1:
                    t[l] += v
                    if l < size: dd[l] += v
                    l += 1
                if r & 1:
                    r -= 1; t[r] += v
                    if r < size: dd[r] += v
                l >>= 1; r >>= 1
            build(l0); build(r0 - 1)
        else:
            l = int(d[k + 1]) - 1 + size; r = int(d[k + 2]) + size; k += 3
            push(l); push(r - 1)
            m = INF
            while l < r:
                if l & 1:
                    if t[l] < m: m = t[l]
                    l += 1
                if r & 1:
                    r -= 1
                    if t[r] < m: m = t[r]
                l >>= 1; r >>= 1
            cnt += 1
            res = (res + cnt * m) % MOD
    print(res)
main()

title: Distinct Visitors
description:
A museum logs the visitor ID of each of its N entries. Auditors ask Q questions: how many distinct visitors entered between entry l and entry r (inclusive)?

Building a set per query is O(N) each. Sort the queries by r and keep only the last occurrence of every ID marked in a Fenwick tree.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N, Q ≤ 40000
  • 1 ≤ idi ≤ 109
  • 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ N

Input

The first line contains N, the second the N IDs, the third Q, and then Q lines l r.

Output

Let ans1, ans2, …, anst be the answers to the questions, in order. To keep the output small, print a single integer: the checksum (1·ans1 + 2·ans2 + … + t·anst) mod 1000000007, taken as a non-negative remainder (exactly what Python's % gives). If t = 0, print 0.

Example

Input:
6
1 2 1 3 2 2
4
1 6
2 4
5 6
3 3

Output:
16

In this example the individual answers are 3, 3, 1, 1, so the checksum is 1·3 + 2·3 + 3·1 + 4·1 mod 1000000007 = 16.
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(d[0]); a = d[1:1 + n]
    q = int(d[1 + n]); p = 2 + n
    L = [0] * q; Rr = [0] * q
    for i in range(q):
        L[i] = int(d[p]); Rr[i] = int(d[p + 1]); p += 2
    qo = sorted(range(q), key=Rr.__getitem__)
    B = [0] * (n + 1)
    last = {}
    ans = [0] * q
    cur = 0
    for qi in qo:
        r = Rr[qi]
        while cur < r:
            cur += 1
            v = a[cur - 1]
            pl = last.get(v, 0)
            if pl:
                i = pl
                while i <= n:
                    B[i] -= 1; i += i & -i
            i = cur
            while i <= n:
                B[i] += 1; i += i & -i
            last[v] = cur
        s = 0; i = r
        while i > 0:
            s += B[i]; i -= i & -i
        i = L[qi] - 1
        while i > 0:
            s -= B[i]; i -= i & -i
        ans[qi] = s
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    print(sum((i + 1) * v for i, v in enumerate(ans)) % MOD)
main()

title: Top Performers in Every Window
description:
A league records the scores a1 … aN of N consecutive matches. For every window of W consecutive matches, the committee sums the K largest scores in that window (if values repeat, each occurrence counts separately).

Sorting every window is far too slow for large W. Maintain the window in a Fenwick tree over value ranks (counts and sums) and walk it with binary lifting — or use two heaps with lazy deletion.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ K ≤ W ≤ N ≤ 30000
  • |ai| ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains N W K; the second line contains the N scores.

Output

Let ans1, ans2, …, anst be the answers to the N - W + 1 windows from left to right (ansi = sum of the K largest scores in window i), in order. To keep the output small, print a single integer: the checksum (1·ans1 + 2·ans2 + … + t·anst) mod 1000000007, taken as a non-negative remainder (exactly what Python's % gives). If t = 0, print 0.

Example

Input:
6 3 2
5 1 4 -2 8 3

Output:
99

In this example the individual answers are 9, 5, 12, 11, so the checksum is 1·9 + 2·5 + 3·12 + 4·11 mod 1000000007 = 99.
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, W, K = int(d[0]), int(d[1]), int(d[2])
    a = list(map(int, d[3:3 + n]))
    order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: (a[i], i))
    rk = [0] * n
    for r, i in enumerate(order): rk[i] = r + 1
    C = [0] * (n + 1); S = [0] * (n + 1)
    LOG = 1
    while LOG * 2 <= n: LOG *= 2
    m = W - K
    total = 0
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    res = 0; cnt = 0
    for i in range(n):
        x = a[i]; j = rk[i]; total += x
        while j <= n:
            C[j] += 1; S[j] += x; j += j & -j
        if i >= W:
            y = a[i - W]; j = rk[i - W]; total -= y
            while j <= n:
                C[j] -= 1; S[j] -= y; j += j & -j
        if i >= W - 1:
            pos = 0; rem = m; acc = 0; step = LOG
            while step and rem:
                np_ = pos + step
                if np_ <= n and C[np_] <= rem:
                    pos = np_; rem -= C[np_]; acc += S[np_]
                step >>= 1
            cnt += 1
            res = (res + cnt * (total - acc)) % MOD
    print(res)
main()

title: Most Chaotic Window
description:
A queue of N people has heights a1 … aN. The chaos of a group of consecutive people is the number of inversions in it: pairs of positions i < j in the group with ai > aj (strictly; equal heights are not an inversion). Among all windows of exactly W consecutive people, find the maximum chaos and the window where it happens.

Recounting each window is O(W log W) or worse. When the window slides, only the inversions involving the removed and the added person change.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ W ≤ N ≤ 50000
  • 1 ≤ ai ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains N W; the second line contains the N heights.

Output

Print two integers separated by a space: the maximum chaos, and the 1-based starting position of the window achieving it. If several windows tie, print the smallest starting position.

Example

Input:
6 3
3 1 2 5 4 1

Output:
3 4
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, W = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    a = list(map(int, d[2:2 + n]))
    vals = sorted(set(a))
    idx = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(vals)}
    rk = [idx[v] for v in a]
    D = len(vals)
    B = [0] * (D + 1)
    inv = 0
    for i in range(W):
        r = rk[i]; s = 0; j = r
        while j > 0:
            s += B[j]; j -= j & -j
        inv += i - s
        j = r
        while j <= D:
            B[j] += 1; j += j & -j
    best = inv; bs = 1
    for i in range(W, n):
        r = rk[i - W]; j = r
        while j <= D:
            B[j] -= 1; j += j & -j
        s = 0; j = r - 1
        while j > 0:
            s += B[j]; j -= j & -j
        inv -= s
        r = rk[i]; s = 0; j = r
        while j > 0:
            s += B[j]; j -= j & -j
        inv += (W - 1) - s
        j = r
        while j <= D:
            B[j] += 1; j += j & -j
        if inv > best:
            best = inv; bs = i - W + 2
    print(best, bs)
main()

title: Tour Groups and Hotels
description:
A road has N hotels; hotel i (counting from the city gate) has hi free rooms. M tour groups arrive one by one; group j needs rj rooms and they must all be in the same hotel. Each group takes the first hotel from the gate that still has at least rj free rooms, and those rooms become occupied. If no hotel has enough rooms, the group leaves (answer 0).

Scanning hotels from the gate for every group is O(N·M). Descend a max-segment-tree instead.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N, M ≤ 60000
  • 1 ≤ hi, rj ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains N M, the second the free rooms h1 … hN, the third the requests r1 … rM.

Output

Let ans1, ans2, …, anst be the answers to the groups (ansj = 1-based index of the hotel group j stays in, or 0), in order. To keep the output small, print a single integer: the checksum (1·ans1 + 2·ans2 + … + t·anst) mod 1000000007, taken as a non-negative remainder (exactly what Python's % gives). If t = 0, print 0.

Example

Input:
8 5
3 2 4 1 5 5 2 6
4 4 7 1 1

Output:
22

In this example the individual answers are 3, 5, 0, 1, 1, so the checksum is 1·3 + 2·5 + 3·0 + 4·1 + 5·1 mod 1000000007 = 22.
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, m = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    size = 1
    while size < n: size *= 2
    t = [0] * (2 * size)
    for i in range(n): t[size + i] = int(d[2 + i])
    for p in range(size - 1, 0, -1):
        a = t[2 * p]; b = t[2 * p + 1]; t[p] = a if a > b else b
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    res = 0
    for g in range(m):
        need = int(d[2 + n + g])
        if t[1] < need:
            ans = 0
        else:
            p = 1
            while p < size:
                p *= 2
                if t[p] < need: p += 1
            ans = p - size + 1
            t[p] -= need
            p >>= 1
            while p:
                a = t[2 * p]; b = t[2 * p + 1]; t[p] = a if a > b else b
                p >>= 1
        res = (res + (g + 1) * ans) % MOD
    print(res)
main()

A lab has N samples with unknown masses m1 … mN. It processes Q records in order:

  • 1 x y w: a technician claims my - mx = w. If this contradicts the claims accepted so far, the claim is rejected (and counted as a contradiction); otherwise it is accepted. (A claim with x = y is consistent exactly when w = 0.)

title: Smallest Missing Ticket
description:
A cinema handed out N tickets in a row; ticket i has the number ai (numbers are non-negative and may repeat). For each of Q queries l r, find the MEX of al … ar: the smallest non-negative integer that does not appear among them.

Process queries offline by r; in a segment tree indexed by value, store the last position where each value appeared, and descend to the first value whose last position is before l.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N, Q ≤ 50000
  • 0 ≤ ai ≤ 109
  • 1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ N

Input

The first line contains N, the second the N ticket numbers, the third Q, followed by Q lines l r.

Output

Let ans1, ans2, …, anst be the answers to the queries, in order. To keep the output small, print a single integer: the checksum (1·ans1 + 2·ans2 + … + t·anst) mod 1000000007, taken as a non-negative remainder (exactly what Python's % gives). If t = 0, print 0.

Example

Input:
7
0 1 2 0 3 1 4
4
1 7
2 4
2 3
5 7

Output:
11

In this example the individual answers are 5, 3, 0, 0, so the checksum is 1·5 + 2·3 + 3·0 + 4·0 mod 1000000007 = 11.
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(d[0]); a = list(map(int, d[1:1 + n]))
    q = int(d[1 + n]); p = 2 + n
    L = [0] * q; Rr = [0] * q
    for i in range(q):
        L[i] = int(d[p]); Rr[i] = int(d[p + 1]); p += 2
    size = 1
    while size < n + 2: size *= 2
    t = [0] * (2 * size)
    qo = sorted(range(q), key=Rr.__getitem__)
    ans = [0] * q
    cur = 0
    for qi in qo:
        r = Rr[qi]
        while cur < r:
            cur += 1
            v = a[cur - 1]
            if v <= n:
                j = size + v; t[j] = cur; j >>= 1
                while j:
                    x = t[2 * j]; y = t[2 * j + 1]; t[j] = x if x < y else y
                    j >>= 1
        l = L[qi]; j = 1
        while j < size:
            j *= 2
            if t[j] >= l: j += 1
        ans[qi] = j - size
    MOD = 10**9 + 7
    print(sum((i + 1) * v for i, v in enumerate(ans)) % MOD)
main()
